messages:
Alice (sales): Hey team — FinTechCo wants clarification on regional endpoints and KMS for a POC. They require EU-only data egress and prefer keys managed in the EU. Is that doable on Hosted? Any sub-processor concerns?
Mike (solutions): Short answer: hosted supports routing preferences but not hard-geofencing. We can route by default to eu-west region, but fallback behavior will cross regions if capacity is constrained unless we pin.
Mike (solutions): Options: 1) Hosted + routing policy (soft affinity) — easiest, cheaper, can be configured today. 2) Dedicated capacity in EU — guaranteed, supports EU-only egress and EU KMS. 3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full control.
Jorge (arch): For Hosted, sub-processor footprint in EU is limited — our cloud infra vendors + CDN + monitoring partners. We have a published subprocessors list: https://docs.redwood.ai/subprocessors (send link). If customer needs EU-only sub-processors, Dedicated/Private is recommended.
Alice (sales): Claire — security questionnaire flagged "Where are keys stored?" and "Do you use any non-EU sub-processors for request handling?" Can you confirm wording we can send back?
Claire (security): We can confirm: keys for Hosted use our KMS in the selected region; for EU pinning we can use EU KMS via Dedicated or Private. Hosted may store backups or logs in the region but some control-plane metadata may transit other regions — we need to check the specific SSF entries. I'll prepare a paragraph.
Nina (finance): Pricing note: Dedicated with EU KMS adds a baseline uplift — roughly +25% on the instance commit and a small per-request KMS usage fee. If they need hard pinning / no cross-region fallback, that's a commit-level SLA.
Alice (sales): Customer also asked: if we pin to eu-west, what happens during outages? Will requests fail or route to us-east?
Mike (solutions): If pinned to Dedicated EU pool with SLA, we failover only to other EU capacity (we can set a failover policy to keep within EU). On Hosted soft-affinity, we may route to nearest available region (could cross-border). We can include a canary + alerting plan in the POC.
Jorge (arch): Quick config snippet customers like: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-2", "region": "eu-west-1", "routing": { "pin": true, "failover": "eu-only" } }
```
(This is logical — actual API flags might differ; SE should confirm with infra).
Mike (solutions): Action items: 1) Claire to draft security text re: KMS/subprocessors. 2) Nina to give an estimated uplift number for Dedicated/EU KMS. 3) I will draft a POC runbook (routing config, test plan, traffic mix).
Claire (security): Will do. Also need the customer's legal contact and their required subprocessors list to map against ours — ask FinTechCo to share their vendor whitelist.
Nina (finance): I can rough a number by EOD — ballpark: Dedicated EU baseline $12k/mo + incremental kms/egress. Will refine after SE traffic profile.
Alice (sales): Thanks. Mike — can you also include a short test to prove no cross-border egress? Customer wants screenshots for controls audit.
Mike (solutions): Yep — we'll do a traffic-capture test from the POC and a signed attestation. I'll add it to the runbook.
infra-bot: deployment-notice: created POC env redwood-poc-fintechco-eu at 2026-03-21T14:58:02Z :rocket:
Alice (sales): Great — looping in customer (cc @FinTechCo-security) to say we’re working on the questionnaire and pricing. Will share updates as soon as Claire/Nina/Mike confirm. :thumbsup:
